title: Runtime 1.3 to Runtime 2.0: what actually breaks
purpose: Fabric runtime migration. Component version changes; Library re-publish requirement; JAR recompilation; ANSI mode default flip; Delta protocol interoperability; Rollback path.
accessibleSummary: Fabric runtime migration. Component version changes; Library re-publish requirement; JAR recompilation; ANSI mode default flip; Delta protocol interoperability; Rollback path.
longDescription: Fabric runtime migration. Component version changes; Library re-publish requirement; JAR recompilation; ANSI mode default flip; Delta protocol interoperability; Rollback path.

nodes.label: Component versions move together
nodes.summary: Six component layers move at once between Runtime 1.3 and Runtime 2.0.
nodes.detail: Six component layers move at once between Runtime 1.3 and Runtime 2.0.
nodes.whyItMatters: Six component layers move at once between Runtime 1.3 and Runtime 2.0.

evidence.note: Runtime 1.3 carries Spark 3.5.5, Delta 3.2, Java 11, Scala 2.12.17 and Python 3.11; Runtime 2.0 carries Spark 4.1, Delta 4.2, Java 21, Scala 2.13.16 and Python 3.13.

processing: Compare component versions across the move
outputs: A list of breakage surfaces to test
drill.example: Python moving from 3.11 to 3.13 alone invalidates every installed wheel.
failureModes: Treating the move as a single version bump underestimates six simultaneous changes.

nodes.label: Production stays on GA
nodes.summary: Microsoft's guidance is production on GA, with Runtime 2.0 piloted separately.
nodes.detail: Microsoft's guidance is production on GA, with Runtime 2.0 piloted separately.
nodes.whyItMatters: Microsoft's guidance is production on GA, with Runtime 2.0 piloted separately.

evidence.note: Microsoft's guidance is to run production workloads on the most recent GA runtime, currently Runtime 1.3.
Runtime 2.0 is Public Preview while Runtime 1.3 is GA.

drill.example: A dedicated pilot workspace runs Runtime 2.0 while production stays on 1.3.
failureModes: Moving production to a preview runtime accepts preview-level support for critical pipelines.

nodes.label: Libraries must be re-published
nodes.summary: The Python version jump requires libraries to be re-added and published.
nodes.detail: The Python version jump requires libraries to be re-added and published.
nodes.whyItMatters: The Python version jump requires libraries to be re-added and published.

evidence.note: Library migration works when Python and R versions are unchanged; a conflicting library can fail the environment build outright.

processing: Export, re-add and publish libraries on the target runtime
outputs: A working library set on Runtime 2.0
drill.example: An unexported library list leaves a team reconstructing dependencies by trial and error.
failureModes: A build conflict blocks the whole Environment, not just the offending package.

nodes.label: JVM artifacts need recompiling
nodes.summary: Scala and Java version changes require custom JARs to be recompiled.
nodes.detail: Scala and Java version changes require custom JARs to be recompiled.
nodes.whyItMatters: Scala and Java version changes require custom JARs to be recompiled.

evidence.note: JARs have a significant chance of not working because Scala, Java, Spark and the operating system all change.

drill.example: A custom connector JAR built for Scala 2.12 fails to load on the new runtime.
failureModes: Re-uploading the same artifact appears to succeed until the class fails to load at run time.

nodes.label: ANSI mode flips on
nodes.summary: Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, turning silent NULLs into runtime errors.
nodes.detail: Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, turning silent NULLs into runtime errors.
nodes.whyItMatters: Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, turning silent NULLs into runtime errors.

evidence.note: Spark 4.x turns ANSI on by default and the Native Execution Engine falls back to JVM under ANSI.
ANSI SQL mode always executes on JVM Spark rather than the native path.

processing: Enable ANSI on Runtime 1.3 and run the test suite
outputs: A list of ANSI-sensitive code paths
drill.example: A divide-by-zero that returned NULL on 3.5 raises a runtime exception on 4.x.
failureModes: Discovering ANSI breakage in production rather than in a pre-flight test on the current runtime.

nodes.label: Delta protocol interoperability
nodes.summary: Delta 4.x-only features raise the table protocol irreversibly and can break other readers.
nodes.detail: Delta 4.x-only features raise the table protocol irreversibly and can break other readers.
nodes.whyItMatters: Delta 4.x-only features raise the table protocol irreversibly and can break other readers.

evidence.note: Calling delta.upgradeTableProtocol raises the protocol irreversibly and can leave existing readers or writers unable to access the table.

drill.example: Enabling a Delta 4.x-only feature on a gold table breaks the SQL analytics endpoint reading it.
failureModes: The protocol upgrade cannot be undone, so an untested enablement is permanent.

nodes.label: Verify native execution afterwards
nodes.summary: Native execution must be verified after migrating because ANSI forces fallback.
nodes.detail: Native execution must be verified after migrating because ANSI forces fallback.
nodes.whyItMatters: Native execution must be verified after migrating because ANSI forces fallback.

evidence.note: An untouched Runtime 2.0 environment with NEE enabled may be running almost entirely on the JVM.
The Fabric Spark Advisor surfaces real-time alerts when execution falls back to JVM-based Spark.

outputs: Confirmed native execution or a known fallback
drill.example: A migrated job shows no native operator suffixes, revealing that ANSI silently disabled acceleration.
failureModes: Assuming the engine is accelerating a workload that is entirely on the JVM.

nodes.label: Rollback is a config change
nodes.summary: Runtime is an Environment-level setting, so rollback is a configuration change.
nodes.detail: Runtime is an Environment-level setting, so rollback is a configuration change.
nodes.whyItMatters: Runtime is an Environment-level setting, so rollback is a configuration change.

evidence.note: The runtime version is set at the workspace or Environment item level and applies from the next session.

drill.example: A failing pilot reverts by pointing notebooks back at the 1.3 Environment.
failureModes: Deleting the old Environment removes the rollback path and turns a pilot into a commitment.

edges.label: Scala and Java changes force recompilation
Delta version enables new table features
ANSI fallback must be verified in the plan
Piloting depends on a working rollback
